England primary maths · Year 1

Year 1 maths.
Stronger basics, one match at a time.

Counting and numbers to 100. Bonds, addition and subtraction to 20. Equal groups, halves, quarters, measures and shapes. Use the academy alongside teaching and practical learning.

Build a Year 1 player

What does Year 1 practice focus on?

01

Counting and numbers to 100

02

Bonds, addition and subtraction to 20

03

Equal groups, halves, quarters, measures and shapes

The map below names 30 practice families available for this year. Supporting skills can be revisited when a pupil needs them. Schools may sequence content differently within a key stage.

The Year 1 skills map

Number

Count to 100

Count forwards and backwards across 100; steps of 2, 5 and 10.

Count the objects

Connect pictures, quantities and numerals.

One more, one less

Find a neighbouring number.

Numbers and words to 20

Connect numerals and number names.

More, fewer, equal

Compare numbers and quantities.

Add & subtract

Addition within 10

Little numbers. A strong start.

Subtraction within 10

Take away and find what is left.

Make 10

Find the two parts that make 10.

Addition across 10

Make 10, then add the rest.

Subtraction across 10

Step back to 10, then keep going.

Make 20

Build on the bonds you already know.

Doubles & halves

Two equal parts, both ways round.

Missing numbers

Use what you know to find the gap.

Addition to 20

Add one- and two-digit numbers within 20, including zero.

Subtraction to 20

Subtract within 20, including zero.

Find the missing number

Find missing values in different equation positions.

One-step number stories

Choose a calculation from a short context.

Times & divide

Equal groups

Use pictures and repeated addition.

Share equally

Share small quantities into equal groups.

Fractions & decimals

Halves and quarters

Recognise equal halves and quarters of a shape.

Half or quarter of a set

Find equal parts of a quantity.

Measure & time

Compare measures

Compare length, mass, capacity and time.

Coins and notes

Recognise UK coin and note values.

Days, months and order

Sequence events and use calendar vocabulary.

Hours and half hours

Read hour and half-hour clock faces.

Set the clock

Construct hour and half-hour times.

Shapes & space

Name 2D shapes

Recognise shapes in different orientations.

Name 3D shapes

Recognise common solids.

Position and direction

Use left, right, above, below and between.

Turns

Whole, half, quarter and three-quarter turns.

Recall and connections

Groups before recall

Begin with pictures, equal groups, sharing, doubles and counting in 2s, 5s and 10s. A timed multiplication table target comes later.

Times-table guide

Beyond a number answer

A grown-up records practical and reasoning work alongside digital practice.

  • Measure real objects
  • Make equal parts
  • Draw clock hands
  • Handle shapes and describe a route
  • Explain a number story

How Year 1 promotion works

XP rewards effort and independent answers, but does not award a completed year. The academy checks broad independent coverage and later-day recall across this year’s families. Practical observations are recorded by a grown-up. A 12-shot promotion match then requires at least 90% independent accuracy, with the other goals still satisfied. Earlier facts remain available for review after promotion.

This is an in-game progression policy. It is not a DfE-approved pass mark, a diagnostic judgement or a guarantee that a skill will never be forgotten.
